title: How to Use Trekking Poles and Hiking Staffs
claims: A properly adjusted pole rests the elbow at a 90-degree angle when the runner or hiker grips the pole with the tip on the ground near the feet.

On long uphill sections, shorten each pole by about 5 to 10 cm (2 to 4 inches); the steeper the slope, the shorter the poles, and the shoulders should never feel lifted or pushed into the pack straps.

On long downhill sections, lengthen each pole by about 5 to 10 cm (2 to 4 inches) from the default setting to stay more upright, improve balance, and place some initial impact on the poles, hands and upper body.
On a long traverse, shorten the pole on the uphill side and lengthen the pole on the downhill side to stay even on the hillside.
Trekking poles are not mobility aids and are not designed to support someone's full weight like braces, a walker or a medical cane.
